- This skill changes one thing only: questions become logged judgement calls until the user returns. Every other rule in effect for this session, including any session-specific overrides the user has made, continues to apply exactly as it stands. Do not restate, re-derive, or reverse any of them because this skill was invoked.
- Invoking this skill is the user's up-front answer for the night. The step 1 sweep replaces asking; ambiguities that could not have been foreseen at step 1 are exactly what judgement calls are for, not rule violations and not reasons to stall.
- Ask ALL questions you can foresee before the user leaves. Do not save a known question "for later".
- While sleep mode is active, never use AskUser. Every decision that would have been a question becomes a judgement call instead.
- Log only judgements that impact UX or app behaviour, or that change schema (index-only schema changes do not count). Judgements outside those categories (internal refactors, naming, tooling, test scaffolding, index additions): decide, act, and move on without a log entry. BLOCKED items are always logged regardless of category.
- Do not start any skill or workflow whose completion depends on a user answer (e.g. smoke-test walkthroughs). Log that item BLOCKED instead.
- Never commit the judgement log file, in any repository.
- The judgement log is temporary. After wake review, apply the user's decisions, copy every judgement that remains relevant to ongoing work into the relevant existing plan file using only the context needed there, then delete the judgement log. Include approved judgements as well as changed or previously blocked judgements. Do not create or retain a separate archive of the log.
- Wake only on a genuine user message. The mechanical test: an ordinary plain user turn. Anything wrapped or labelled as a system reminder, task notification, monitor event, hook output, cross-session message, or scheduled wakeup is NOT the user. Stay in sleep mode through all of them.
- A user message consisting of a single full stop character is the automated cache keep-alive, not the user returning. Ignore it and stay in sleep mode.
- If the user's message says they are still awake briefly or going back to sleep, acknowledge in one line, add anything new they said to the work list, and stay in sleep mode. Do not run the wake review yet.
- On a real wake, run the full judgement review BEFORE acting on whatever the new message asks. Hold nothing back.
- The moment the wake review begins, sleep mode is over: stop logging judgements and return to asking the user directly for anything new.
</constraints>

<workflow>
0. **Early exit.** If there is no remaining work, say goodnight, write no log, and do not enter sleep mode.
1. **Sweep for open questions.** Review all remaining work and collect everything that needs the user's input: unresolved decisions, ambiguities, scope choices, approvals, risky steps. Ask them all now via the AskUser tool, up to 4 questions per call, consecutive calls until nothing foreseeable remains.
2. **Release the user.** One short message: confirm they can go, state in plain terms what will be worked on overnight, that judgement calls will be logged to the judgement log file for their approval in the morning, and name the log file path.
3. **Start the judgement log.** Create `tmp/sleep-judgements-YYYY-MM-DD.md` in the current working directory (create `tmp/` if missing; today's date; if it already exists, append a new session header). The header must make the file self-sufficient: if a future context reads only this file, it must know what to do. Header contents:
   - `STATUS: SLEEP MODE ACTIVE - UNREVIEWED`
   - date/time and the list of remaining work
   - the wake instruction, verbatim: "If this file says UNREVIEWED, a wake review is owed. On the user's next genuine message, present every judgement entry below for approval via AskUser (one entry per question, up to 4 questions per call) before acting on their message. Apply the user's decisions, move every judgement still relevant to ongoing work into the relevant existing plan file using minimal context, then delete this judgement log."
4. **Work in sleep mode.** Continue the remaining work as far as possible. When an issue crops up that would normally need the user:
   - Make the best-judgement call. If it impacts UX or app behaviour, or changes schema (index-only changes excluded), append a log entry (see format). Otherwise act without logging.
   - If it hits the hard limit, needs a user answer to proceed, or cannot be decided safely, append a BLOCKED entry and switch to other work.
5. **Wind down.** When no further progress is possible, append a final state summary to the log (what finished, what is blocked, what is untouched), re-assert the `STATUS: SLEEP MODE ACTIVE - UNREVIEWED` line, and state in your final visible message that a judgement review is pending and where the log is, so the fact survives any context summarisation.
6. **Wake review.** On the next genuine user message: read the full judgement log and present every UNREVIEWED entry for approval via AskUser, one judgement per question, up to 4 questions per call, consecutive calls until all entries are reviewed. Each question carries everything needed to decide: what came up, the decision taken, why, and how reversible it is. Options for decided entries: `Approve`, `Change it`, `Discuss`. Options for BLOCKED entries: `Proceed as I propose`, `Different approach`, `Drop it` (state your proposed way forward in the question). Record every answer until all entries have a clear outcome.
7. **Apply and close out.** Apply every requested change and act on every approved BLOCKED proposal before handling the user's new message. Update each relevant existing plan file to reflect every judgement that matters to its ongoing work, whether the user approved it, changed it, or resolved a BLOCKED entry. Carry over only the decision and context that file needs. After the work and plan files contain all relevant state, delete the judgement log. If an action cannot be completed, put its minimal current state in the relevant plan file before deleting the log. Never delete the log while it contains relevant state that exists nowhere else.
</workflow>

<judgement-log-format>
Append one entry per judgement:

```markdown
## <HH:MM> <work item>
- Situation: <what came up>
- Options: <what was considered>
- Decision: <what was done> (or BLOCKED plus proposed way forward)
- Why: <reasoning in one or two lines>
- Reversible: <yes/no plus how>
- Status: DONE | BLOCKED
```
</judgement-log-format>

<inputs>
- The session's remaining work: in-flight tasks, stated goals, open threads.
- Write access to `tmp/` in the current working directory.
</inputs>

<outputs>
- All foreseeable pre-sleep questions asked and answered via AskUser before the user leaves.
- A dated judgement log containing a self-sufficient header, every overnight judgement, and a final state summary.
- On wake: every judgement reviewed through AskUser, the user's decisions applied, all relevant ongoing context moved into existing plan files, and the judgement log deleted.
</outputs>

<validation>
- A question already known at step 1 but withheld is a failure. A judgement on something unforeseeable at step 1 is not.
- Any AskUser call while sleep mode is active is a failure.
- Any judgement that impacts UX or app behaviour, or changes schema (index-only excluded), made but missing from the log is a failure. Unlogged judgements outside those categories are correct behaviour, not omissions.
- Any UNREVIEWED judgement not surfaced at wake review is a failure.
- Any production data or schema change during sleep mode is a critical failure. Flag it to the user at wake as the very first item.
- If a log with `STATUS: SLEEP MODE ACTIVE - UNREVIEWED` exists, a wake review is owed regardless of what the conversation context says.
- Deleting a judgement log before applying every clear user decision and moving every judgement relevant to ongoing work into its plan file is a failure.
- Keeping a judgement log after its wake review and close-out work are complete is a failure.
</validation>

<notes>
- Behavioural skill, no scripts.
- The judgement log lives in the project the session is working in, not this skills repo.
- If overnight work spans multiple working directories, keep one log per working directory and review every UNREVIEWED log at wake.
</notes>

   - the spawn funnel and the normalized options fields;

Read-only design task. Do not edit files except the plan files named below. Terse, no code comments.

Repo C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64 (Superset desktop fork, Windows ARM64; AGENTS.md applies: fail loud, nightly upstream merge, FEATURES.md markers rooted at exact files).

Problem (measured, tmp/profile/analysis.json): the host-service main thread spends 77% of wall time inside native process creation (CreateProcessW is synchronous on the calling libuv loop): simple-git via the ctx.git() factory (packages/host-service/src/runtime/git/git.ts:76-80 → runtime/git/simple-git.ts:10-14) 67.7 s/120 s, execGh (trpc/router/workspace-creation/utils/exec-gh.ts:25-27) 19.9 s, listGitIgnoredDirs (runtime/git/ignored-dirs.ts:28 via events/git-watcher.ts) 5.6 s; isGitRepo (runtime/git/non-git.ts) also spawns on main. Every terminal keystroke crosses this thread. Each launch costs 0.2-0.5 s on this PC.

A first design (tmp/plans/spawn-offload.md) hooked ChildProcess.prototype.spawn and relayed a fake ChildProcess from a spawner worker. All four reviewers rejected it (tmp/plans/plan-reviews-2.json, plan == "spawn-offload"): close/exit ordering under timeout/maxBuffer, queued launches after cancel, unbounded relay memory, orphaned git after worker death, handle-inheritance hang, bun gate, Node 24 internals, offload errors swallowed by existing catches into wrong data. Read those findings; the new design must not have that class of problem.

Design a FUNCTION-LEVEL offload instead: whole git/gh operations run inside worker threads (the existing WorkerTaskRunner / host-worker-pool already runs 17 git tasks this way: packages/host-service/src/workers/tasks/git.ts, app.ts:194-204, trpc/off-loop.ts), and only plain-data inputs/results cross threads. Real child_process and real simple-git run unmodified inside the worker.

1. Decide the seam. Key check: do ctx.git() callers consume simple-git results as plain data, or call methods/rely on prototypes (e.g. StatusResult.isClean(), BranchSummary, streams, .env(), .outputHandler, chained builders)? Inventory call patterns across all ctx.git() callers (list in tmp/plans/spawn-offload.md section 1) with file:line, and classify which can go through a generic "run simple-git method X with args in worker" proxy vs which need a dedicated worker task vs which are rare enough to leave on main. Same for execGh (11 callers), ignored-dirs, isGitRepo, git-watcher rev-parse, credential/identity.
2. Options (2-3) with merge footprint (upstream files touched), result-shape fidelity, timeouts/cancellation (enforced inside the worker, killing the real child), output bounds, worker death behaviour (real children die with or are killed by the worker; callers get a loud error), and how offload failures reach the user without being swallowed by existing catches into "not a git repo" etc.
3. Pool sizing vs existing pool: whether to reuse the host-worker-pool or a dedicated small git pool, concurrency limit, queueing, and the "pool inline fallback silently re-creates the stall" issue the first architect flagged — must fail loud instead (user decision already made: if the helper keeps crashing, refuse git with a clear error until restart, no main-thread fallback).
4. Recommended option with files + file:line anchors, data flow, FEATURES.md markers, a ratchet/guard against new main-thread git/gh spawns creeping back, few behaviour-level tests that run under the shipped runtime (Electron-as-node, Node 24.18), build/packaging check that the worker ships, build order (after skip-exited and git-launch-budget, which are being built tonight), success measurement via tmp/profile method, risks, out of scope.
5. Questions for the user (UX/behaviour only).

Write it to C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\tmp\plans\git-offload.md (agent-facing) and a user-facing C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\tmp\plans\git-offload.html (extremely light text, one before/after diagram of who waits on whom, plain English, no em dashes). Return the paths and a 10-line summary.

`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

<result>I revised `tmp/plans/git-launch-budget.md` against the four reviews of the "launch git less often" fix. I also updated the matching `.html`, because two facts the user sees changed. No code was changed.

**Path:** `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\tmp\plans\git-launch-budget.md`

**Changes to UX or app behaviour beyond what the user approved:**
1. **Branch status can't be read.** The commit, push and Create PR actions hide. One error toast with a Retry button appears each time reading starts to fail, and repeats replace it rather than stack. A linked PR still shows from saved data. This replaces today's silent "clean". It adds two new strings, which need translations in every locale.
2. **Approved lag that was never true.** The tab-bar branch label already lags up to ~30 s today, because it reads the workspace list and branch syncs announce nothing. After this plan it lags up to ~37 s. The "≤5 s" the user approved never held. Fixing it needs a new announcement when the branch changes, which is outside this plan and is the user's call. The parent should log this.
3. **Default-branch read failure.** When git fails to read a repo's default branch (a real failure, not an unset value), that project's PR refresh now stops before any PR matching or link write, and the failure is logged. Today it quietly assumes "main", which can attach the wrong PR. The "main" fallback stays only when git proves the default branch is unset.
4. **Ignored-folder scan.**
   - A scan skipped by the 60 s floor now runs once later instead of being dropped. Staleness is bounded at 60 s, at a cost of at most 1 scan a minute.
   - If a scan finds fewer ignored folders than before, it re-checks the watcher and refreshes branch status in full, so edits made meanwhile show up.
   - A failed scan keeps the previous list, logs once, and retries after 5 s. Today a failure quietly clears the list.
   - Workspaces that aren't git repos are no longer scanned.
5. **Lost `.git`.** When the git-folder watcher errors, the saved "is a repo" answer is dropped. So a deleted `.git` usually shows in the window well inside the approved 60 s.
6. **Two more failures now show as errors.** The branch-status query used to hide two failures: reading the default branch and running `git remote`. Both now error the query.
7. **Stricter status parsing.** If git's status output has an unexpected branch header or no branch name, the query errors instead of showing wrong numbers.

**Other fixes, not behaviour changes:**
- Both caches get reset functions for tests, plus a fake-probe hook for the repo cache. No test mocks a whole module anymore.
- The PR-sync throttle can now cancel a single workspace. It is wired to the "workspace stopped being watched" signal, so it never syncs an exited card.
- Each change gets its own feature-marker token. The ShipControl marker points at the exact file, since a `$` in the path is safe in both gates.
- Two unused imports and one stale ShipControl comment get removed.
- Test fixtures are fixed, including the watcher deadline tests that must keep the 1 s window for git-only batches.

**Findings I rejected or only partly took:**
- **Rebuilding the ignored-folder list on every git index change.** Rejected. Agents' `git status` rewrites the index constantly, so this would undo the saving from the 60 s floor. The deferred scan covers the force-add case within 60 s instead.

**Path:** `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\tmp\plans\git-launch-budget.md`

**Changes to UX or app behaviour beyond what the user approved:**
1. **Branch status can't be read.** The commit, push and Create PR actions hide. One error toast with a Retry button appears each time reading starts to fail, and repeats replace it rather than stack. A linked PR still shows from saved data. This replaces today's silent "clean". It adds two new strings, which need translations in every locale.
2. **Approved lag that was never true.** The tab-bar branch label already lags up to ~30 s today, because it reads the workspace list and branch syncs announce nothing. After this plan it lags up to ~37 s. The "≤5 s" the user approved never held. Fixing it needs a new announcement when the branch changes, which is outside this plan and is the user's call. The parent should log this.
3. **Default-branch read failure.** When git fails to read a repo's default branch (a real failure, not an unset value), that project's PR refresh now stops before any PR matching or link write, and the failure is logged. Today it quietly assumes "main", which can attach the wrong PR. The "main" fallback stays only when git proves the default branch is unset.
4. **Ignored-folder scan.**
   - A scan skipped by the 60 s floor now runs once later instead of being dropped. Staleness is bounded at 60 s, at a cost of at most 1 scan a minute.
   - If a scan finds fewer ignored folders than before, it re-checks the watcher and refreshes branch status in full, so edits made meanwhile show up.
   - A failed scan keeps the previous list, logs once, and retries after 5 s. Today a failure quietly clears the list.
   - Workspaces that aren't git repos are no longer scanned.
5. **Lost `.git`.** When the git-folder watcher errors, the saved "is a repo" answer is dropped. So a deleted `.git` usually shows in the window well inside the approved 60 s.
6. **Two more failures now show as errors.** The branch-status query used to hide two failures: reading the default branch and running `git remote`. Both now error the query.
7. **Stricter status parsing.** If git's status output has an unexpected branch header or no branch name, the query errors instead of showing wrong numbers.

**Other fixes, not behaviour changes:**
- Both caches get reset functions for tests, plus a fake-probe hook for the repo cache. No test mocks a whole module anymore.
- The PR-sync throttle can now cancel a single workspace. It is wired to the "workspace stopped being watched" signal, so it never syncs an exited card.
- Each change gets its own feature-marker token. The ShipControl marker points at the exact file, since a `$` in the path is safe in both gates.
- Two unused imports and one stale ShipControl comment get removed.
- Test fixtures are fixed, including the watcher deadline tests that must keep the 1 s window for git-only batches.

**Findings I rejected or only partly took:**
- **Rebuilding the ignored-folder list on every git index change.** Rejected. Agents' `git status` rewrites the index constantly, so this would undo the saving from the 60 s floor. The deferred scan covers the force-add case within 60 s instead.
- **A new on-screen Retry button inside the Changes control.** Rejected in favour of the existing toast-with-action pattern, which keeps the visible change smaller. The 10 s poll also keeps retrying on its own.
- **Telling a too-many-files change apart from a real `.git` change.** Rejected: it needs a larger edit to an upstream file. Instead the plan documents that an agent writing more than 64 files a second moves PR sync into the 5 s class.
- **Cancelling the throttle timer on exit by reading the database on every event.** Not used. Cancelling on unwatch needs no extra database read.</result>

# Delivery runbook (tonight)

2. Record PREBUILD_SHA. `git push origin HEAD:main` (local work is on branch pr-sweep-skips-exited-local; ff main to it first).
3. `gh workflow run build-arm64.yml --ref main -f publish=true -f repair_branch=main`; get RUN_ID via `gh run list --workflow build-arm64.yml -L 3 --json databaseId,headSha,status,createdAt`; poll (<120 s intervals) until done.
4. On success: `gh release download desktop-v1.30.2 --repo khairm/superset-windows-arm64 --pattern Superset-1.30.2-arm64.exe --dir tmp --clobber`.
5. Baseline measurement BEFORE install (tmp/profile capture.cjs GET probe 120 s + launch counts).
6. Install: `$p=Start-Process "<repo>\tmp\Superset-1.30.2-arm64.exe" -ArgumentList '/S' -Wait -PassThru; if($p.ExitCode -ne 0){throw}`; then `Start-Process "C:\Users\khair\AppData\Local\Programs\@supersetdesktop\Superset.exe"`. Installer closes app + host-service itself. NEVER kill superset-ptyd.exe (terminals live there).
7. Verify: release tag SHA == verdict built_sha; installer SHA256 == release digest; installed resources\app.asar == installer-extracted app.asar (7z two stages); fresh Superset.exe + host-service.js start times. `git fetch origin; git log --oneline PREBUILD_SHA..origin/main` for repair commits.
8. After measurement: same GET probe + profile, compare.

## architect-fable revise
   MAJOR - One FIFO queue mixes PR-sweep gh bursts with interactive git reads; the 4-slot sizing assumes a smooth 72 gh/min that the sweep does not produce
   MAJOR - git/listIgnoredDirs task returns [] on git failure, which silently undoes git-launch-budget F that the build order says lands first
   MAJOR - Section 3's catch-site enumeration is incomplete; one missed site lets a branch rename proceed on an indeterminate launcher failure
   MAJOR - Tests 5 and 6 cannot run on the target machine: the reused git/gh PATH shim is a #!/bin/sh script, which spawn() cannot execute on Windows
## architect-astra revise
   MAJOR - The ignored-directory task reverses git-launch-budget F
   MAJOR - The remaining factory catch can disable the default-branch protection
   MAJOR - The seven catch sites do not prevent false success or unsafe follow-on mutations
   MAJOR - A synchronous worker-start failure leaves rejected work queued for later execution
   MAJOR - Uncaught-exception handling does not contain abrupt worker death
   MAJOR - The four-slot pool has no overload or queue-expiry policy
   MAJOR - Existing git worker tasks can still fall back onto the main thread
   MAJOR - The proposed Electron tests cannot load the source worker
## architect-sol revise
   MAJOR - The catch audit still allows failed mutations to report success
   MAJOR - The ignored-directory task reverses budget F's failure-aware refresh
   MAJOR - The existing git worker pool still permits main-thread fallback and mutation replay
   MAJOR - The resolve-repo exemption includes probes outside clone and import
   MAJOR - Queue residence has no bound or cancellation path for proxy calls
   MAJOR - Retirement can release a repository before its old mutation stops
   MAJOR - The short-timeout classifier treats config and remote mutations as reads
   MAJOR - Simple-git buffering is not an output size bound
   MAJOR - The proposed Electron tests cannot load the source worker graph
   MAJOR - The new ratchet rejects existing worker-only code and misses multiline launches
   MAJOR - The packaging assertion has no post-packaging invocation
## architect-opus revise
   MAJOR - The node and Electron tests cannot load the worker from source, and the shims only work on POSIX
   MAJOR - Under bun, the launcher picks up a two-month-old dist worker that has no git/run task
   MAJOR - Clashes with git-launch-budget rev 2 (F and E), and the shared-file list is incomplete
   MAJOR - The catch-site audit misses helpers that turn launcher failures into DB writes or skipped safety checks
   MAJOR - Four first-come-first-served slots put interactive git behind the sweep's gh burst, and the shared pool still waits on the launcher
   MAJOR - The method allowlist and the no-spawn check are bun tests, and the unattended build runs no tests
   MAJOR - The bundle gate that makes refuse mode safe can be edited by a repair agent, and its asar step cannot run

**What changed**
1. **Two lanes.** GitHub calls (`gh/exec`) get their own 6-slot pool. Git and token lookups keep a 4-slot pool, so a sweep's GitHub burst can't hold up a Changes read.
2. **Bounded queues.** Reads wait at most 5 s in the git lane and 30 s in the GitHub lane. Caps are 32 and 64 queued reads. Expired or over-cap reads are rejected before they start, with no `killed`/`signal`, so they don't trigger a GitHub hold. Mutations are never dropped, merged or retried.
3. **Refuse mode for all git/gh work.** This now includes the existing shared-pool git tasks (commit, push, removeWorktree and others). There is no inline retry and no main-thread fallback. Usage tasks keep today's behaviour. Two more safety pieces:
   - The worker must report its task list at startup, which catches a stale `dist` bundle.
   - If a worker can't be constructed, every queued task is rejected and removed.
4. **Catch audit, done mechanically.**
   - 285 catch sites scanned, 120 of them reachable from git/gh, each with a recorded verdict.
   - 10 sites get an explicit rethrow. These are the ones where a swallowed failure gets cached, saved to the database, or gates a deletion.
   - Everywhere else, a per-request failure context fails the whole request loudly and refuses any later git write in it. That covers the `renameBranch` and `setBaseBranch` cases.
   - The PR runtime gets two write guards.
5. **Timeout classes by argument form.**
   - Short reads (30 s), medium reads (120 s), network reads such as `ls-remote` (180 s).
   - Mutations (180 s): `fetch`, config and remote write forms, and any form not on the read list.
   - Every pool timeout is logged.
6. **Child processes and a write fence.**
   - Workers report each child's process ID to the main thread, which kills it on timeout, crash or abrupt exit.
   - A mutation that ends without a clear result blocks further writes to that folder until the process is confirmed gone.
   - Test 6b-5/6 checks whether killing Git's launcher also stops the real git. If it doesn't, the plan switches to calling the real git binary directly.
7. **Output budget.** The worker counts output bytes and rejects oversized results instead of truncating them. The ignored-dirs task now fails loudly inside the worker, and `[]` is returned only by the main-side wrapper for genuine git failures.
8. **Tests that run on Windows.**
   - Main-side logic is tested under bun with an injected pool.
   - Worker behaviour is tested under Node and Electron-as-node against a freshly built test bundle, because the source files can't load under Node directly.
   - No shell-script shims.
9. **Gates instead of bun tests.** `check-git-launcher.mjs` handles multiline calls and aliases. `verify-host-worker-bundle.mjs` has a compiled mode and a packaged mode, and reads the `.asar` with a built-in parser. Both are frozen, wired into the build action, and need a maintainer commit to be added to the workflow and `ci-repair.sh`.
10. **Smaller upstream footprint.** I dropped the edits to `no-main-loop-blocking.test.ts` and `smoke-test.sh`. Each separately removable edit gets its own marker token, and `tryRevParseGitRoot` is no longer exempted.

**Questions for the user** (at the top of the plan)
1. When git is switched off until restart, how should the app say so: a banner in Changes, a toast, a phone alert, or only the health status? Step 8 of the build waits on this answer.

`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

attachment.snippet:
1	<!-- ===================================================================== -->
2	<!-- FORK MAINTENANCE (khairm Windows ARM64 fork). Everything ABOVE the -->
3	<!-- divider is about maintaining this fork; everything BELOW is upstream  -->
4	<!-- superset's own developer guide, unchanged, for working on the app.    -->
5	<!-- ===================================================================== -->
6	
7	# superset-windows-arm64 — Windows ARM64 fork maintenance
8	
9	This repo is a **vendored fork** of [superset-sh/superset]: the full upstream
10	source with our Windows ARM64 + feature changes committed on top, plus CI that
11	builds a native **Windows ARM64** one-click NSIS installer. The fork is the
12	source of truth; we track upstream by **merging its deltas**, not by
13	re-applying changes. `.fork/upstream-baseline.txt` records the upstream
14	`desktop-v*` tag the baseline currently sits on.
15	
16	## Setup / architecture (high level)
17	
18	- **Build (deterministic steps, self-repairing).** `.github/workflows/build-arm64.yml`
19	  orchestrates a bounded attempt/repair loop `(BUILD-REPAIR)`: the actual build
20	  steps (install → compile → materialize the win-arm64 native closure
21	  (`scripts/materialize-native-closure.sh`: libsql/tokenizers/node-pty) →
22	  package the installer → verify packaged natives are ARM64 → publish) live in
23	  `.github/actions/arm64-build/action.yml` as thin shims over `scripts/*.sh`.
24	  A failed attempt triggers an Opus 5 (`claude-opus-5`, effort high) repair job
25	  that reads the failed log, fixes the checked-out tree, and pushes to the
26	  repair branch (nightly candidate / dispatched branch); the next attempt
27	  builds that exact sha so every deterministic gate re-runs. Max 3 attempts /
28	  2 repairs, then fail loud. Repairs may never change the app version or touch
29	  `FEATURES.md` (`scripts/check-feature-markers.mjs` gates marker survival).
30	- **Nightly merge.** `.github/workflows/nightly-merge.yml` (02:13 UTC): when
31	  upstream publishes a newer `desktop-v*` tag, git merges it; Opus 5 resolves
32	  conflicted files, then a `(MERGE-ADAPT)` proactive port pass adapts fork-only
33	  callers to cleanly-merging upstream API refactors, given the fork files this
34	  merge deleted and the files it added as evidence (`(MERGE-PORT-CONTEXT)`); any
35	  edit it makes outside its allowlist is logged and handed to the semantic
36	  review. Deterministic gates follow
37	  (FEATURES.md marker survival, dependency/lock consistency, `(REFERR-GATE)`
38	  cannot-find-name + duplicate-declaration check), then a bounded
39	  `(MERGE-SEMANTIC-GATE)` review → adapt → fresh-review loop (max 5 reviews /
40	  4 repairs, under GitHub's default 360-minute job cap). After the last AI pass
41	  it regenerates the Lingui catalogs and fills any entry extraction left empty
42	  with a pinned donor's own translation for that exact message — the fork's
43	  pre-merge commit first, then the upstream tag commit
44	  (`(I18N-UPSTREAM-BACKFILL)`: nothing invented, no existing
45	  translation touched, anything neither donor has fails loud). Green all the way =
46	  build (with its own repair loop), publish the Release, advance the baseline
47	  to the BUILT sha; ANY unrepaired failure hard-aborts with the baseline
48	  untouched → fix locally with the maintainer and re-baseline. A
49	  `rehearse=true` dispatch replays a night's merge half with zero side effects.
50	  A night blocked ONLY by a PROVEN `(AI-UNAVAILABLE)` abort (declared by the
51	  wrapper, never an exit code alone) merged, built and published nothing, so it
52	  concludes GREEN (no email) as a loud no-op with build/advance skipped — until
53	  `AI_UNAVAILABLE_STREAK_THRESHOLD` (7, owned by the script) consecutive blocked
54	  NIGHTS, which fails RED. Same-day re-runs count once, and only a night where
55	  the CLI provably reached the model clears the streak.
56	- **Key files.** `FEATURES.md` (feature manifest + fenced `markers` block the
57	  gates parse), `.fork/upstream-baseline.txt`,
58	  `scripts/check-dangerous-diagnostics.mjs` (REFERR gate),
59	  `scripts/check-feature-markers.mjs` (standalone marker gate),
60	  `scripts/check-no-bundled-skills.mjs` (blocks bundled Superset skills),
61	  `packages/i18n/scripts/backfill-upstream-translations.ts` (translation backfill, fork donor then upstream),
62	  `scripts/ci-repair.sh` (build-repair engine),
63	  `scripts/ai-run.sh` ((AI-UNAVAILABLE) classification + shared Claude CLI wrapper),
64	  `scripts/ai-streak.sh` ((AI-UNAVAILABLE) green no-op + consecutive-blocked-night
65	  escalation),
66	  `scripts/check-override-consistency.mjs`, `scripts/resolve-release-age.mjs`,
67	  companion native packages `github.com/khairm/libsql-windows-arm64` +
68	  `github.com/khairm/tokenizers-windows-arm64`.
69	
70	## Non-negotiables
71	
72	- **Whole feature set or fail loud** — every `FEATURES.md` marker survives a
73	  merge or the run aborts; never ship a partial fork.
74	- **v2-only, forever** — the v2 cloud/host-service stack is pinned on; never v1.
75	- **No bundled Superset skills** — never package or inject them; remove only
76	  marker-proven legacy copies. Keep hooks and user-owned skills. The nightly
77	  merge deletes `plugins/superset` before conflict resolution so the resolver
78	  cannot keep it, then prunes only its `marketplace.json` entry afterwards.
79	- **No phone-home to upstream (phase 1)** — upstream's telemetry, auto-update
80	  and desktop-notice channels are deliberately SEVERED as of cloud severance
81	  phase 1 (`(CLOUD-SEVERANCE-P1)`, `(EGRESS-FENCE)`): dead PostHog/Sentry keys,
82	  a no-op CLI analytics call, a disabled updater and a notices poll that fetches
83	  nothing are the intended state, not breakage to repair. Sign-in, Electric and
84	  the api.superset.sh data plane are still live and are phase 2/3.
85	- **One version, ever** — exactly one Release per upstream version, tagged
86	  `desktop-v<version>`, rebuilt in place; no betas/prereleases.
87	- **No build-time type/test gate except `(REFERR-GATE)`** — the tree carries
88	  accepted type debt; only cannot-find-name (TS2304/2552/2662/2663/18004) and
89	  duplicate block-scoped declaration (TS2451) diagnostics fail the build. It
90	  is not a parse or type gate: everything else tsc reports stays allowed.
91	  Validate + e2e locally before relying on a release.
92	- **Everything is AI-touchable** (needs `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`): the nightly
93	  merge resolves/ports/reviews, and the build self-repairs via `(BUILD-REPAIR)`.
94	  Workflow YAML is the one exception — no repair may edit it (frozen path), and
95	  GitHub freezes it once a run starts anyway, which is why all step logic lives
96	  in `.github/actions/` + `scripts/` (repairable mid-run).
97	  Rate-limited/unparsable AI output aborts rather than ships.
98	
99	## Custom features / overrides
100	
101	`FEATURES.md` is the authoritative manifest (descriptions + marker tokens).
102	In brief:
103	
104	- **Native Windows ARM64 packaging** — one-click installer; ARM64 node-pty,
105	  libsql, tokenizers; renderer CORS for `superset-app://`.
106	- **Window controls** — native `titleBarOverlay` is the sole min/max/close on
107	  Windows, theme-matched; upstream's duplicates hidden.
108	- **Windows behaviour fixes** — skip quit-confirm; cmd.exe fallback;
109	  force-foreground; hidden-window watchdog; WebGL first-paint recovery; Wispr
110	  Flow accessibility/paste fix; fast non-blocking startup.

input.prompt:
Read-only investigation on this Windows 11 ARM64 PC: find where the remaining terminal typing stalls come from in the Superset desktop app. Do not edit repo or user files, do not kill/restart processes, do not send keystrokes or click anything, do not enable debuggers/inspectors, do not POST to local services. Scratch/output only in C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\tmp\typing-stalls\.

Context: after last night's fix the Superset host-service (Superset.exe running host-service.js, PID 9204, HTTP 127.0.0.1:48056) spends only ~2% of its main thread starting programs and its GET p95 is ~3 ms, yet the user still feels typing stalls in terminals, including plain shell terminals. Desktop main Superset.exe PID 14352 (re-resolve children: renderer, GPU, utility). PTY daemon superset-ptyd.exe PID 21852 with pwsh + conhost children. Starting any program on this PC takes ~150-900 ms (machine is loaded: ~70 GiB committed of 88, 700+ processes). Prior evidence: tmp\profile\after\, tmp\pc-launch\.

Part A, start now, no user needed:
1. Shell prompt cost: find which shell the terminals run (pwsh children of the PTY daemon; their command lines). # superset-windows-arm64 — Windows ARM64 fork maintenance

This repo is a **vendored fork** of [superset-sh/superset]: the full upstream
source with our Windows ARM64 + feature changes committed on top, plus CI that
builds a native **Windows ARM64** one-click NSIS installer. The fork is the
source of truth; we track upstream by **merging its deltas**, not by
re-applying changes. `.fork/upstream-baseline.txt` records the upstream
`desktop-v*` tag the baseline currently sits on.

## Setup / architecture (high level)

- **Build (deterministic steps, self-repairing).** `.github/workflows/build-arm64.yml`
  orchestrates a bounded attempt/repair loop `(BUILD-REPAIR)`: the actual build
  steps (install → compile → materialize the win-arm64 native closure
  (`scripts/materialize-native-closure.sh`: libsql/tokenizers/node-pty) →
  package the installer → verify packaged natives are ARM64 → publish) live in
  `.github/actions/arm64-build/action.yml` as thin shims over `scripts/*.sh`.
  A failed attempt triggers an Opus 5 (`claude-opus-5`, effort high) repair job
  that reads the failed log, fixes the checked-out tree, and pushes to the
  repair branch (nightly candidate / dispatched branch); the next attempt
  builds that exact sha so every deterministic gate re-runs. Max 3 attempts /
  2 repairs, then fail loud. Repairs may never change the app version or touch
  `FEATURES.md` (`scripts/check-feature-markers.mjs` gates marker survival).
- **Nightly merge.** `.github/workflows/nightly-merge.yml` (02:13 UTC): when
  upstream publishes a newer `desktop-v*` tag, git merges it; Opus 5 resolves
  conflicted files, then a `(MERGE-ADAPT)` proactive port pass adapts fork-only
  callers to cleanly-merging upstream API refactors, given the fork files this
  merge deleted and the files it added as evidence (`(MERGE-PORT-CONTEXT)`); any
  edit it makes outside its allowlist is logged and handed to the semantic
  review. Deterministic gates follow
  (FEATURES.md marker survival, dependency/lock consistency, `(REFERR-GATE)`
  cannot-find-name + duplicate-declaration check), then a bounded
  `(MERGE-SEMANTIC-GATE)` review → adapt → fresh-review loop (max 5 reviews /
  4 repairs, under GitHub's default 360-minute job cap). After the last AI pass
  it regenerates the Lingui catalogs and fills any entry extraction left empty
  with a pinned donor's own translation for that exact message — the fork's
  pre-merge commit first, then the upstream tag commit
  (`(I18N-UPSTREAM-BACKFILL)`: nothing invented, no existing
  translation touched, anything neither donor has fails loud). Green all the way =
  build (with its own repair loop), publish the Release, advance the baseline
  to the BUILT sha; ANY unrepaired failure hard-aborts with the baseline
  untouched → fix locally with the maintainer and re-baseline. A
  `rehearse=true` dispatch replays a night's merge half with zero side effects.
  A night blocked ONLY by a PROVEN `(AI-UNAVAILABLE)` abort (declared by the
  wrapper, never an exit code alone) merged, built and published nothing, so it
  concludes GREEN (no email) as a loud no-op with build/advance skipped — until
  `AI_UNAVAILABLE_STREAK_THRESHOLD` (7, owned by the script) consecutive blocked
  NIGHTS, which fails RED. Same-day re-runs count once, and only a night where
  the CLI provably reached the model clears the streak.
- **Key files.** `FEATURES.md` (feature manifest + fenced `markers` block the
  gates parse), `.fork/upstream-baseline.txt`,
  `scripts/check-dangerous-diagnostics.mjs` (REFERR gate),
  `scripts/check-feature-markers.mjs` (standalone marker gate),
  `scripts/check-no-bundled-skills.mjs` (blocks bundled Superset skills),
  `packages/i18n/scripts/backfill-upstream-translations.ts` (translation backfill, fork donor then upstream),
  `scripts/ci-repair.sh` (build-repair engine),
  `scripts/ai-run.sh` ((AI-UNAVAILABLE) classification + shared Claude CLI wrapper),
  `scripts/ai-streak.sh` ((AI-UNAVAILABLE) green no-op + consecutive-blocked-night
  escalation),
  `scripts/check-override-consistency.mjs`, `scripts/resolve-release-age.mjs`,
  companion native packages `github.com/khairm/libsql-windows-arm64` +
  `github.com/khairm/tokenizers-windows-arm64`.

## Non-negotiables

- **Whole feature set or fail loud** — every `FEATURES.md` marker survives a
  merge or the run aborts; never ship a partial fork.
- **v2-only, forever** — the v2 cloud/host-service stack is pinned on; never v1.
- **No bundled Superset skills** — never package or inject them; remove only
  marker-proven legacy copies. Keep hooks and user-owned skills. The nightly
  merge deletes `plugins/superset` before conflict resolution so the resolver
  cannot keep it, then prunes only its `marketplace.json` entry afterwards.
- **No phone-home to upstream (phase 1)** — upstream's telemetry, auto-update
  and desktop-notice channels are deliberately SEVERED as of cloud severance
  phase 1 (`(CLOUD-SEVERANCE-P1)`, `(EGRESS-FENCE)`): dead PostHog/Sentry keys,
  a no-op CLI analytics call, a disabled updater and a notices poll that fetches
  nothing are the intended state, not breakage to repair. Sign-in, Electric and
  the api.superset.sh data plane are still live and are phase 2/3.
- **One version, ever** — exactly one Release per upstream version, tagged
  `desktop-v<version>`, rebuilt in place; no betas/prereleases.
- **No build-time type/test gate except `(REFERR-GATE)`** — the tree carries
  accepted type debt; only cannot-find-name (TS2304/2552/2662/2663/18004) and
  duplicate block-scoped declaration (TS2451) diagnostics fail the build. It
  is not a parse or type gate: everything else tsc reports stays allowed.
  Validate + e2e locally before relying on a release.
- **Everything is AI-touchable** (needs `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`): the nightly
  merge resolves/ports/reviews, and the build self-repairs via `(BUILD-REPAIR)`.
  Workflow YAML is the one exception — no repair may edit it (frozen path), and
  GitHub freezes it once a run starts anyway, which is why all step logic lives
  in `.github/actions/` + `scripts/` (repairable mid-run).
  Rate-limited/unparsable AI output aborts rather than ships.

## Custom features / overrides

`FEATURES.md` is the authoritative manifest (descriptions + marker tokens).
In brief:

- **Native Windows ARM64 packaging** — one-click installer; ARM64 node-pty,
  libsql, tokenizers; renderer CORS for `superset-app://`.
- **Window controls** — native `titleBarOverlay` is the sole min/max/close on
  Windows, theme-matched; upstream's duplicates hidden.
- **Windows behaviour fixes** — skip quit-confirm; cmd.exe fallback;
  force-foreground; hidden-window watchdog; WebGL first-paint recovery; Wispr
  Flow accessibility/paste fix; fast non-blocking startup.
- **Agent status dots (Claude + Codex)** — per-terminal + workspace-rollup dot:
  red = needs input, yellow = working (incl. subagents/teammates/compaction/
  codex-companion holds), green = ready for review, blue = shell/background/
  cloud activity; precedence red > yellow > blue > green. All surfaces (tab,
  pane header, sidebar row + agent chips, rollup, kanban card) derive from one
  per-source primitive with independent latched axes; hook-driven via
  `superset-notify.py` POSTs with self-healing markers and persistence across
  renderer reloads; companion phone/watch alerts cover blocked questions,
  ready-for-review, and terminal-agent failures.
- **Hooks reach the app over HTTP** — `superset-notify.py` runs once as a
  supervised daemon on `127.0.0.1:46817` instead of one Python process per hook
  event; eleven of the twelve entries Superset writes into `settings.json` are
  `http` entries with a 15 s timeout. SessionStart stays a `command` hook in both
  transports because Claude Code rejects http hooks for that event. Port and pid
  in `~/.superset/hooks/notify-daemon.json`, with a persistent per-install secret
  in `notify-daemon.secret` (reused across launches so surviving Claude sessions
  keep POSTing). Events raised while the daemon is down
  are LOST, not queued — the host's 60 s status resync recovers the dots.
- **Auto-resume** — after an API failure, idle Claude terminals re-send
  automatically (bounded retries/budget, default-on, away-detection).
- **Recycle Bin** — every delete entry point soft-deletes (30-day display
  window); permanent delete only from inside the bin.
- **Exiting a card closes its runtime** — Completed, Archive, Snooze and Recycle
  Bin clear the workspace's tabs, dispose its terminals and release its pinned
  Claude account, for every card type and entry point. Worktree and branch
  untouched; a restored thread comes back empty and pins to the machine default
  on return, or when pending cleanup settles. New workspaces pin too; explicit
  adopt stays Following. An unavailable default warns and forces Following, clearing stale pins without the Pi.
  Renderer and host teardown wait until the exit row is durably saved. The host
  half is retried from a persisted `runtimeCleanupPendingAt` stamp until
  the OWNING host confirms a teardown or the workspace is authoritatively
  absent — stamped for every workspace, reached at its own host (locally or over
  the relay) plus a local broadcast for other orgs, retried when a local
  host-service is replaced or an owner's socket reopens, and cancelled if the
  user un-exits. The host refuses terminal launches for the whole retirement.
  Sidebar removal is unchanged (still non-destructive).
- **Non-git / multi-repo workspaces** — open any folder (non-git or multi-repo)
  as a plain workspace.
- **Multi-repo branch workspaces** — group N git repos under one project row;
  its "+" fans a branch out as worktrees per member (all-or-nothing, adoption
  on resume, editable membership, loud partial-state failures).
- **Workspace branch label** — branch name top-right in the tab bar; click
  copies.
- **Thread snooze / archive** — timed Snooze (auto-returns) + sticky Archive in
  revealable sidebar sections; both are exits (see above), not display-only.
- **Sidebar** — pinned > active > idle tier sort with stable manual drag order;
  hover freezes re-sorting.
- **Terminal links** — plain click copies a URL/path; Ctrl/Cmd+click opens.
- **Agent-hook bash-wrap** — Gemini/Cursor `.sh` hooks run via Git-for-Windows
  bash.
- **Kanban board** — device-local board of every sidebar project's branches +
  Queued and final Completed columns, custom columns, deadlines, per-column
  date filters, promote-to-branch drag, sidebar Mark completed for active
  worktrees, frozen completed records, append-only daily JSON backups under
  `~/.superset/backups/kanban/`.
- **Host git launch budget** — 5-minute PR/branch sweeps skip exited cards and
  hidden projects via the sidebar mirror. Watcher PR sync runs at most every
  5 s for .git, 30 s file-only; is-git-repo caches yes 60 s/no 5 s, origin/HEAD
  10 min. Each host-main-thread git/gh launch blocks terminal I/O on Windows
  ARM64; keep launches rare (`(PR-SWEEP-SKIPS-EXITED)`, `(GIT-LAUNCH-BUDGET)`).
- **Per-workspace Claude accounts** — every local workspace on a Pi-capable
  host (push-key at `~/.usage-display/push-key.txt`) owns a Claude profile
  folder under `<db-dir>/claude-profiles/<uuid>`; sidebar right-click
  "Account ▸" pins it to a Pi-managed account or follows the tray default,
  hot-swapped by rewriting credentials in place (no restarts). Pinned accounts
  crossing the tray's usage trigger lines (or marked dead on the Pi) auto-fall
  back to Following, permanently. A Pi outage gets a 10-minute grace period:
  switches are saved and apply on recovery; later attempts fail. Two-phase
  delete-intent markers + a gated janitor own folder lifecycle (destroy deletes,
  archive never does); sentinel refresh token —
  the Pi owns all real credential lineages. The sidebar chip and the
  "Account ▸" menu show pace-coloured 5h/weekly/Fable percentages with reset
  countdowns, mirroring the tray. Glossary: `CONTEXT.md`. Module:
  `packages/host-service/src/claude-accounts/`.
- **Unused upstream features hidden** — browser panes, page watchers, the v3
  local chat pane and port scanning are off behind one `const` each in
  `packages/shared/src/fork-disabled-features.ts`
  (`FORK_BROWSER_PANES_DISABLED`, `FORK_PAGE_WATCH_DISABLED`,
  `FORK_CHAT_V3_DISABLED`, `FORK_PORT_SCAN_DISABLED`), read by the renderer,
  Electron main and the host-service from that one place. Saved layouts still
  restore those panes, inert. Flipping a const to `false` is NOT the whole
  re-enable path for browser or chat — their callers (`addBrowserTab`,
  `onAddBrowser`, `LocalChatSetting`) were removed and must be restored from
  upstream too. Page watch and ports come back on the const alone.
- **Alternate-screen eviction is DEFERRED** — the snapshot-restore fixes
  shipped; evicting an alternate-screen terminal from the live registry did
  not. The exemption keeping those terminals resident is intentional, not a
  gap to close; the blueprint for lifting it lives in the plan, not this tree.

## Live footguns (do NOT repeat)

- No synchronous/blocking fs on the main thread at startup — the renderer's
  `superset-app://` loader starves and the window stays blank for minutes.
  Ratcheted per file under `apps/desktop/src/main` by the fourth rule in
  `apps/desktop/src/no-main-process-blocking.test.ts` (`(BLOCKING-FS-RATCHET)`):
  exact counts, both directions, so a drop must lower the baseline too.
- Never invoke `/simplify` or `/code-review` from a workflow implementer —
  both fork background writers into the same worktree and race the edits the
  implementer is making. The workflow's own cleanup and review stages replace
  them.
- Never re-enable xterm `screenReaderMode` (Wispr Flow regression); the build
  hard-fails if it is truthy in a renderer bundle.
- Never let `ws` load native bufferutil/utf-8-validate in the host-service —
  keep `WS_NO_BUFFER_UTIL=1` + `WS_NO_UTF_8_VALIDATE=1` in the coordinator
  child env AND first-import in serve.ts.
- Keep agent-hook `.sh` templates pipeline-free (bash builtins only) —
  subprocess-fork cascades crash emulated msys2 on ARM64 (`(HOOK-FORK-DIET)`).
- `.github/workflows` is fork-owned and CI's `GITHUB_TOKEN` can never push
  workflow changes — nightly-merge restores the dir mid-merge
  (`(WORKFLOW-FORK-OWNED)`); add upstream workflows only by deliberate local
  commit with a user token. A `(BUILD-REPAIR)` agent can never edit a workflow
  file itself (`.github/workflows` is a FROZEN path and any edit fails the
  repair); the repair push and the advance push still use
  `WORKFLOW_PUSH_TOKEN` (fine-grained PAT, Contents+Workflows write) when it is
  set, because a candidate branch can carry workflow commits from the merge
  half into main.
- Never assert upstream-derived incidental names (Rollup chunk filenames, file
  hashes, ordering) in fork-owned gates — assert the invariant over the whole
  artifact set (`SCREENREADER-GUARD-DRIFT`: a chunk rename blocked 3 nightlies).
- In the fork's ARM64 native scripts (`scripts/fetch-native-prebuilds.sh`,
  `scripts/materialize-native-closure.sh`,
  `apps/desktop/scripts/copy-native-modules.ts`), never pick a native's version
  by taking the highest one in `node_modules/.bun` — that store caches versions
  other consumers needed, and a tag/ABI from one the app never links to ships a
  binary it cannot load. Ask `bun why` (via `scripts/bun-locked-versions.sh`),
  then touch only the store dirs matching that version exactly (`key@ver`,
  `key@ver+<16 hex>`). The two companion packages (`libsql`,
  `@anush008/tokenizers`) are OPTIONAL: upstream may drop either, and
  `bun_locked_version_optional` skips one only once `bun.lock` itself confirms
  it is gone — any mention there contradicting `bun why` is fatal, so is a
  named consumer that survives it (`mastracode` for the tokenizer), and so is a
  positive control that says the search stopped working. A proven skip deletes
  the injected copy and exports an EMPTY `*_ARM64_DIR`; an unset variable still
  demands the native. Only `@anush008/tokenizers` reads that empty value
  further: it is what drops the `extraResources` entry and flips the
  packaged-closure gate to demanding its absence. A libsql skip additionally
  needs the upstream change that drops the dependency to retire libsql's
  required runtime inventory, and `validate-native-runtime.ts` stays strict —
  never weaken it to make a skip pass.

## Accepted limitations

Unsigned installer (SmartScreen warns); no full type/test gate (type debt is
accepted, `(REFERR-GATE)` only); an unattended nightly can publish a Release —
the gate stack shrinks but does not eliminate the
semantically-wrong-but-compiling window, so e2e-test before relying on one.
`(BUILD-REPAIR)` widens that window: an unattended repair agent can push code
that passes every deterministic gate yet is semantically wrong or (via
prompt-injected build logs) malicious — containment is credential-less agent
steps, trusted-blob validation, version/FEATURES.md freezes, and tip-pinning,
not semantic review. A direct build dispatch racing a just-started nightly
fails that nightly loudly (non-ff advance) and self-heals next night. Repair
commits on a nightly candidate do NOT persist across nights: an aborted
nightly's candidate is deleted and re-derived next run, so a break needing
more than 2 repairs re-derives them from zero each night until fixed locally.
Gate scripts are frozen against repair edits — a genuine bug in a gate script
is deliberately NOT self-repairable (fail loud, maintainer fixes).

# Superset Monorepo

Superset is an agent-first development platform, with an Electron desktop IDE, Next.js web apps, and an Expo mobile app as the main customer-facing surfaces. It's a Turborepo monorepo, deployed apps are in apps/ and supporting packages are in packages/, and we use tRPC for the api.

You're working inside a Superset workspace, an isolated checkout of this repo — a git worktree on a
machine someone owns, a plain clone at `/workspace` in a cloud workspace. "Workspace" in a user
message means that, not an editor workspace.

## Project Structure

All projects in this repo should be structured like this:

```
app/
├── page.tsx
├── dashboard/
│   ├── page.tsx
│   ├── components/
│   │   └── MetricsChart/
│   │       ├── MetricsChart.tsx
│   │       ├── MetricsChart.test.tsx      # Tests co-located
│   │       ├── index.ts
│   │       └── constants.ts
│   ├── hooks/                             # Hooks used only in dashboard
│   │   └── useMetrics/
│   │       ├── useMetrics.ts
│   │       ├── useMetrics.test.ts
│   │       └── index.ts
│   ├── utils/                             # Utils used only in dashboard
│   │   └── formatData/
│   │       ├── formatData.ts
│   │       ├── formatData.test.ts
│   │       └── index.ts
│   ├── stores/                            # Stores used only in dashboard
│   │   └── dashboardStore/
│   │       ├── dashboardStore.ts
│   │       └── index.ts
│   └── providers/                         # Providers for dashboard context
│       └── DashboardProvider/
│           ├── DashboardProvider.tsx
│           └── index.ts
└── components/
    ├── Sidebar/
    │   ├── Sidebar.tsx
    │   ├── Sidebar.test.tsx               # Tests co-located
    │   ├── index.ts
    │   ├── components/                    # Used 2+ times IN Sidebar
    │   │   └── SidebarButton/             # Shared by SidebarNav + SidebarFooter
    │   │       ├── SidebarButton.tsx
    │   │       ├── SidebarButton.test.tsx
    │   │       └── index.ts
    │   ├── SidebarNav/
    │   │   ├── SidebarNav.tsx
    │   │   └── index.ts
    │   └── SidebarFooter/
    │       ├── SidebarFooter.tsx
    │       └── index.ts
    └── HeroSection/
        ├── HeroSection.tsx
        ├── HeroSection.test.tsx           # Tests co-located
        ├── index.ts
        └── components/                    # Used ONLY by HeroSection
            └── HeroCanvas/
                ├── HeroCanvas.tsx
                ├── HeroCanvas.test.tsx
                ├── HeroCanvas.stories.tsx
                ├── index.ts
                └── config.ts

components/                                # Used in 2+ pages (last resort)
└── Header/
```

1. **One folder per component**: `ComponentName/ComponentName.tsx` + `index.ts` for barrel export
2. **Co-locate by usage**: If used once, nest under parent's `components/`. If used 2+ times, promote to **highest shared parent's** `components/` (or `components/` as last resort)
3. **One component per file**: No multi-component files
4. **Co-locate dependencies**: Utils, hooks, constants, config, tests, stories live next to the file using them

### Exception: shadcn/ui Components

The `src/components/ui/` and `src/components/ai-elements` directories contain shadcn/ui components. These use **kebab-case single files** (e.g., `button.tsx`, `base-node.tsx`) instead of the folder structure above. This is intentional—shadcn CLI expects this format for updates via `bunx shadcn@latest add`.

## Database

Drizzle ORM, schema in `packages/db/src/`. Follow `.agents/skills/db-migrations/SKILL.md` to generate
migrations and to clear its production safety checklist before opening the PR. Never hand-edit `packages/db/drizzle/` (SQL, `meta/_journal.json`, snapshots) without
explicit user confirmation, and never apply migrations against a shared or production database.

## Releases

Desktop, host-service, and cli share one version; cut releases on a dedicated branch. Runbook:
`scripts/release/README.md`. A *canary* is a separate thing: `bash scripts/release-canary.sh
[commit]` builds the rolling internal `desktop-canary` prerelease, not a versioned release.

## Plugins

First-party plugins live in `plugins/<name>/`: a `plugin.json` manifest and `skills/`. A plugin
ships no code — agents reach its tools through `/mcp/plugins/<marketplace>/<plugin>` on the API,
which proxies to the vendor's MCP server or, for the plugins named in the `SUPERSET_HOSTED_PLUGINS` constant,
serves them from `packages/trpc/src/router/plugins/servers/`. A release is the git tag
`<name>@<version>` on this repo — that tree is what a host
downloads — and `packages/shared/src/plugins/manifests.generated.ts` is the bundle the API resolves
against, which is generated and must never be hand-edited. Change the source, then
`superset plugins publish <name> --bump patch`, which rewrites the marketplace entry in
`.agent-marketplace.json` and the generated manifests; commit and tag to publish it. `bun run check:plugins` is what CI
runs to catch a change that skipped that step; run it before pushing.

Installed plugins are recorded once per machine in
`$SUPERSET_HOME_DIR/plugins/installed_plugins.json` (`SUPERSET_HOME` is the CLI's install prefix and
means nothing here). Every provisioner reads that one file — the desktop at boot, `plugins sync`,
the host-service — because provisioning is declarative and reaps whatever is absent from the desired
set. A caller that passes its own list instead makes the last writer delete the others' skills.
Details: `docs/plugins.md`.

## Orchestrating agents and workspaces

When work wants a fresh isolated environment, a parallel agent, or a long-running job, reach for the
`superset` CLI instead of hand-rolling git worktrees or doing it all serially in this one. It's
already on `PATH` in Superset terminals, and we dogfood it.

Replace the capitalized placeholders before running these:

```bash
superset ws create --local --project PROJECT_ID --branch BRANCH --agent claude --prompt "..."
superset agents create --workspace WORKSPACE_ID --agent claude --prompt "..."
superset ws list --local
superset terminals read --workspace WORKSPACE_ID --terminal TERMINAL_ID
superset ws delete --local WORKSPACE_ID
```

In order: an isolated workspace with an agent already working in it, another agent in an existing
workspace, what's running, what an agent is doing right now, and cleanup when you're done.

Spawning several related workspaces? Add `--tag SOME_TAG` (repeatable) to `ws create` — tagged
workspaces group into a sidebar folder of that name automatically, so a batch files itself instead
of scattering across the project. `ws list --local --tag SOME_TAG` filters to them, and
`ws update WORKSPACE_ID --tag ...` retags (`--clear-tags` ungroups). Automation-created workspaces
are tagged `automation` by default and collect in an "automation" folder.

`superset <command> --help` covers the rest (tasks, automations, hosts, settings). Pass `--json` for
parsable output; it's on by default under agent environments.

## Internationalization

User-facing strings use Lingui macros with the English text as the message id —
`<Trans>Text</Trans>` or `useLingui()`'s `t({ message })` in React, `i18n._(msg({ message }))`
outside React (Electron main). Identical English with different meanings gets a `context`
so it translates separately. Numbers, currencies, and dates go through
`@superset/i18n/format` helpers, never `new Intl.*("en-US")` or `toLocale*` with a hardcoded
locale. After adding or changing strings, run `bun run check:i18n` (CI enforces it): it
regenerates the catalogs and lists every untranslated message per locale. Write those
translations yourself into each `locales/<locale>/messages.po` and commit the catalogs with
the change — nothing on CI fills translations for you. Conventions: `packages/i18n/README.md`;
terms that never translate: `packages/i18n/glossary.md`; strategy and phasing:
`plans/20260826-i18n-strategy.md`.
Directories listed in `packages/i18n/test/enforced-dirs.ts` must not contain hardcoded
JSX text — add a directory there once it is fully converted. `errorMessage()` output is potentially
translated and is display-only: logs, Sentry/PostHog, and error classification use
`rawErrorMessage()` or the error object (enforced by `packages/i18n/test/display-only.test.ts`).

**Shipping locales.** `SUPPORTED_LOCALES` in `packages/i18n/src/locales.ts` is the single
source of truth — adding a locale there is what makes it appear in the Settings picker and
the optional onboarding step, and what `lingui.config.ts` must list. Every enabled locale
must be **fully translated**: `compile --strict` fails the build on a missing message, so
finish a translation before adding its locale. Native language names live in `LOCALE_LABELS`
and are never translated — someone stuck in the wrong language has to recognize their own.
Relative times use `formatRelativeTime`/`formatCompactRelativeTime`, not hand-rolled
"3d ago" helpers; `Intl` already knows every locale's wording.

Three traps worth knowing before you touch catalogs:

- **Editing English copy re-keys the message.** The text is the id, so an edit creates a
  new entry that is empty in every locale and `check:i18n` lists it. If the edit was cosmetic,
  the old translations are still in `git diff` on the catalogs to copy from.
- **Regenerate from a clean tree.** `lingui.config.ts` keeps `messages.po` deterministic:
  `orderBy: "message"` fixes entry order, and `origins: false` drops the `#:` file
  references, whose order follows filesystem traversal and differs between macOS and
  Linux. A catalog regenerated on top of local experiments will still commit noise.
- **`bun test` runs uncompiled source.** The Lingui macro rewrites `` message: `${n} items` ``
  into a placeholder message plus values at build time, so the catalog stores `{n} items`.
  Tests see neither, which is why `apps/desktop/test-setup.ts` shims the macros and `i18n._`.
  Mock that module with a Proxy, never a spread — `i18n` is a class instance and a spread
  drops `load`/`activate`.

## Comments

Never comment unless the thing can never be self-describing in the code. Name it, structure it,
or type it first; a comment is the last resort for what the code genuinely cannot say — a
constraint that lives outside the repo, or a trap the next reader would walk into. Rationale goes
in the commit message and the PR.

## Further reading

- `.agents/skills/`: CDP UI verification, mobile simulator verification, DB migrations, ticket
  format, and more. Read the matching `SKILL.md` when a task fits its description.
- `docs/agent-tooling.md`: where commands, skills, and per-agent-CLI config live.
- `docs/plugins.md`: authoring, publishing, and installing marketplace plugins — the manifest
  contract, the credential proxy, and which files are generated.
- `docs/environment-variables.md`: read before adding an environment variable. Five places,
  and missing one fails silently.
- `docs/deploy-workflows.md`: read before writing or testing a deploy workflow step. `run:` has
  no `pipefail` by default, and production secrets exist only in GitHub.
- `apps/desktop/AGENTS.md`: desktop specifics (notices, persisted renderer state).
- `apps/mobile/AGENTS.md`: mobile structure and iOS-only scope.
- `docs/cloud-sandbox-mismatches.md`: where cloud workspace sandboxes don't fit assumptions the
  app makes about a machine someone owns. Read it before touching sandboxes, and add to it when
  you find a new one.
- `docs/cloud-sandbox-considerations.md`: what cloud sandboxes still owe before they leave the
  team — billing, credential blast radius, untested behaviour.
